perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He is a Black male police officer with a high school education. Jonathan Balogun is his childhood best friend, an African American carpenter with a master’s degree; Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his more educated perspective.
- Christian felt Jonathan was hiding something important, became anxious/suspicious, and arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- Christian told Jonathan he felt he was hiding something. He heard Jonathan admit he had been keeping something from him, that he was in some trouble, and that he didn’t know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic, offered help, and said they could face the trouble together. He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated, that he didn’t want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian began to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be criminal. He asked if it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he couldn’t be sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he didn’t do anything illegal himself. Jonathan trusted Christian to look into it discreetly.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. He had leads, planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence, and told Jonathan to hang in there.
- Christian later believed/knew the real culprit was someone close to both him and Jonathan. He told Jonathan he had found out who was behind it, that it was someone they both knew and trusted, and that he would confront them and seek justice. He heard Jonathan warn that the person was dangerous and express trust in him.

Christian does not have access to any private thoughts, hidden facts, or events not stated above, except what he himself observed, was told, or discovered through his investigation.
